comparator.route: Ordinary PPS: four complete modules and 30 EC approved open electives
comparator.sourceNotes: Exact English full-time BA Philosophy specialisation PPS (56081; RIO1015O6460). Current adopted 2026–2027 annual OER, not concurrent prospective years or an old footer date, supplies one coherent ordinary examination framework. 180 EC = B1 compulsory60 + B2/B3 compulsory20 + thesis10 + four complete restricted modules60 + approved open electives30. First-listed semester-compatible distinct module choices are instantiated: Global Justice/Human Rights and Mental Health in autumn, Future of Democracy and Digital Revolution in spring; other modules remain alternatives. No module is counted twice. The 30 EC approved elective option is preserved as two open 15 EC blocks, not invented courses. RADAr English0 is mandatory. Passed Philosophical Writing Workshop precedes Project; passed Project precedes thesis. Seminar/practicum attendance is required. Project assessment is literature20/paper40/presentation20/group bundle20. Thesis5000–6000words; semester1 only for exchange/internship or prior adviser consent. Practice requires attendance, professional reflection and portfolio; presumed module knowledge is not converted into an extra passed-course prerequisite or allowed to erase the formal elective option. Current English and Dutch OER visibly both say BSA44EC, versus prospectus45; adopted rule controls. Specified delayed/later cases60EC. Modules must be complete except applicable transition provisions. The transition body explicitly states2026–2027 despite old2023–24 footers; expired-module exceptions are not used for a new entrant. Future offerings require annual checking.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Actual 2500-year Western philosophy themes, theoretical tools and rigorous critical argument. Substantive philosophical foundation; not three dedicated history courses, philosophy of science or a full metaphysics sequence.
Classical/contemporary thinkers, political power and authority, intellectual presuppositions and normative/empirical connections. Direct political philosophy and argument.
Social institutions and classical/decolonial sociological context, race, gender and class. Sociological foundation, not the full Social and Cultural Philosophy unit.

Moral theories, feminist contributions, practical ethics, equality, animals, climate and historical injustice; independent argumentative essay/project. Direct substantial ethics and philosophical methods.
IR schools/theories and current geopolitical applications, group presentations and Security Council simulation. Political context, not normative international law or philosophical Project.
Actual qualitative design, data, interpretation, dissemination, positionality and group research. Empirical methods, not philosophical textual analysis; retained as complementary inquiry.
Primarily literary stylistics with nonfiction applications, linguistic choices and interpretation. Complementary language analysis; not philosophical writing workshop.
Comparative political institutions and empirical analysis of democracy, authoritarianism, parties, media and globalisation. Political-science complement; not a full philosophy-of-democracy module.
Modern sociology, imperial/colonial context, theory and modernity. Placed before contemporary social theory in both retained routes to respect its assumed content sequence.
Legal systems and cases plus social/normative law-and-justice questions. Complementary interdisciplinary application, not a full philosophical module.

Self-contained classical rhetoric, argumentation canons and essay/presentation skills. Actual autumn offering; replaces advanced persuasion in primary. Partial rhetorical correspondence, not all PPS logic/textual methods.

Historical/contemporary philosophy of mind, selves, Buddhist self-theory, mind-body debate, consciousness, AI and animal minds. Direct philosophical substance; not a dedicated general metaphysics or intercultural-philosophy sequence.
Public international legal sources, force, war, refugee/environmental law and treaty politics. Legal complement, not Philosophy of International Law equivalence.
Conflict theories, inequality, colonial/identity grievances and peacebuilding through travelling concepts. Applied context for ethical/political reflection, not dedicated philosophical ethics of war.

Actual philosophical and psychological inquiry into AI fairness, bias, privacy, accountability, moral status, agency and existential/political implications. Direct philosophical substance, not a full technology/surveillance module.

Current profile documents philosophical argument about free will, responsibility, luck, time, agency and selfhood, including historical perspectives and independent argumentative essays. Direct advanced philosophy; not a complete dedicated metaphysics sequence.
EU actors, institutions, decisions and legislative-dossier/interest-group research. Applied political inquiry, not philosophical history.

Gramsci, Habermas, Fraser, civil society, solidarity, global/decolonial critiques and NGO/CSO research. Actual profile assumes introductory and modern sociology; both now precede it. Not history of contemporary philosophy.

Positive human-rights law and philosophical/historical rights, natural law, Plato/Aquinas/Hobbes/Locke and cases. Genuine mixed philosophical/legal contribution, not full global-distributive-justice module.
Philosophy of emotion: nature, rationality, moral motivation, politics and art through historical/contemporary sources. Direct advanced philosophical inquiry, not generic sociology or a thesis.
Comparative constitutional/administrative principles, powers, democracy, rights and rule of law. Legal and institutional inquiry, not philosophical metaphysics or a complete democracy module.
Actual governance actors, interests, public opinion and enforcement with problem-based food/water/energy/climate cases. Applied political context, not career-portfolio Philosophy in Practice.
Social-movement theory and environmental-justice cases, feminism, anticolonialism and civic engagement. Applied societal context, not a complete decolonial/feminist philosophy sequence.
Climate drivers, natural and social impacts, justice, governance and mitigation/adaptation. Scientific context for ethical inquiry; not all its credit is philosophical study.
Substantial film history, form and cultural analysis, with a brief wider-media introduction. Actual foundation for retained environmental media and documentary study.
Climate communication, contested texts/media and a public-debate project. Direct environmental communication contribution, not a complete environmental-ethics module.
Substantive environmental humanities: Anthropocene, animals, deep time, indigenous/decolonial media, agency, scale and responsibility; final paper/media project. Central to environmental route.
US race, history, representation, oppression/resistance and research podcasts. Distinct media/power contribution, not generic global philosophy or environmental science.

Documentary history, social contexts, ethics/aesthetics, short documentary production and essay exam. Builds coherently on film/media study; practical representation work, not PPS thesis or general philosophy.
Psychological and neuroscientific accounts of learning, personality, mental disorders and treatments establish the empirical foundation for evaluating accounts of mind and illness.
Social cognition, self-concepts, influence, prejudice and interpersonal relationships provide concrete psychological accounts of mental life in social settings.
Research design, operationalisation, measurement and inference supply methods for critically evaluating empirical mental-health claims.
Multivariable models, experimental designs and assumption checks support critical appraisal of behavioural and clinical evidence.
Attention, memory, emotion, consciousness and brain dysfunction supply specific cognitive mechanisms for philosophical questions about mental life.

Historical views, psychiatric classification and biopsychosocial explanations across the lifespan directly support inquiry into competing accounts of mental disorder; no complete neurodiversity or psychiatric-philosophy sequence is claimed.
Developmental theories, attachment, ageing and developmental psychopathology supply a lifespan account of mental life and care; adult interview work is not child clinical training.

Propositional and predicate logic, quantifiers and proof provide formal argument-analysis tools for the philosophical reasoning strand. Discrete mathematics and computation extend beyond that function; no equivalence to full philosophical textual methods is claimed.
Biopsychosocial health, stress, pain, illness and cultural/clinical-health formulation support analysis of how lived and social contexts affect health and care.

Clinical assessment, test validity, diagnostic integration and major psychotherapies provide substantive psychological knowledge of mental-health classification and intervention; this is introductory training, not professional qualification.
Systematic review, risk-of-bias assessment, effect sizes and R meta-analysis provide research-synthesis methods for evaluating empirical mental-health claims.
The description explicitly supports language processing, acquisition, impairment and thought-language relationships, offering a specific cognitive contribution to accounts of mental life.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, politics and public life
alternatives.concept: Philosophy and political thought form the foundation for examining ethics, mind, free will, emotions, public power and justice. Sociology, law and political research connect these questions to contemporary institutions and public life. This is a substantial philosophical and applied political response, with less philosophical history, philosophy of science, dedicated metaphysics and sustained philosophical research than Radboud PPS.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual philosophical foundation and the distinct applied course content support this qualified label.
progression: The fixed six-term schedule has24unique courses, four per semester and Year1PPD. Introductory and modern sociology precede contemporary social theory; formal prerequisite and offering checks pass. No film/media sequence is claimed for this alternative.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, environment and public communication
alternatives.concept: Philosophical ethics, mind, selfhood, emotions, political authority and AI provide the core for studying ecological responsibility and public communication. Climate science, environmental media, climate communication, governance, social movements and documentary work supply a distinct applied cultural and environmental direction. These applied courses do not reproduce dedicated PPS philosophical modules or its thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual philosophical foundation and the distinct applied course content support this qualified label.
progression: Actual workbook term offerings and formal prerequisites checked; modern sociology precedes contemporary social theory. Introductory film precedes the environmental media/documentary sequence. No assumed rhetoric is required before a course without it.
alternatives.distinctness: Six different courses, 45 EC, sustain an environmental/media/communication direction beyond the shared philosophical, sociological and political foundation.

alternatives.label: Mind, mental health and philosophical inquiry
alternatives.concept: A philosophical and mental-health route studies mind, emotion, agency and moral responsibility alongside historical and biopsychosocial approaches to mental disorder, clinical assessment and treatment. Cognitive science, empirical methods and social theory make competing accounts of mental life available for critical inquiry. Clinical courses provide complementary psychological study rather than a dedicated philosophy-of-psychiatry or neurodiversity sequence, and do not confer a clinical qualification.
alternatives.labelReason: Five dedicated philosophy courses, political philosophy and AI ethics are combined with clinical psychology, mind/brain study and empirical methods. The label names that actual combination without claiming clinical or specialist psychiatric-philosophy qualification.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes all formally dependent cognitive and clinical courses. Psycholinguistics uses its documented Spring2027 offering. Research/statistics precedes experimental methods and evidence synthesis. Introductory sociology precedes modern sociology. Logic adds formal argument analysis alongside the clinical and empirical perspectives. All fixed-term offerings and formal prerequisites are validated.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces political institutions, legal study and environmental/media applications with sustained clinical, cognitive, lifespan and methodological study of mental life. The common philosophical foundation supports different questions and substantive course selections; the differences are consequences of the mental-health concept rather than swaps for a numerical floor.

candidates.label: Technology, ecological change and political ethics
candidates.reason: Shared52.5EC direct philosophy/political philosophy/AI substance plus distinct environmental humanities, communication, science and governance contributions. No full PPS-module equivalence.

candidates.label: Global justice, human rights and democracy
candidates.reason: Primary already substantively covers political philosophy, rights, institutions and justice. The original third route added only one further law course; empire history, sociology and poetry did not establish a sufficiently distinct sustained global-justice/democracy organisation. Its formal four-course difference alone did not prove academic distinctness.

candidates.label: Mental health, selfhood and psychiatric crisis
candidates.reason: Renewed review of current course evidence establishes a coherent philosophical/clinical/cognitive response. Psychopathology explicitly covers historical, diagnostic and biopsychosocial perspectives; philosophy of mind, emotion, agency and ethics supplies substantive philosophical inquiry. The distinct clinical and methodological curriculum does not assert full specialist-module equivalence or clinical qualification.

candidates.label: Human sociality and animal life
candidates.reason: Human-animal relations and biopolitics remain an evidenced PPS direction. The selected philosophy/mind and environmental courses supply partial related content; no fourth programme is generated after three verified alternatives.

candidates.label: Intercultural and decolonial philosophy
candidates.reason: Intercultural/decolonial philosophy remains independently evidenced. Sociology and media supply related perspectives, with limits of disciplinary framing; the three-alternative maximum has been reached.

candidates.label: Gender, sexuality and feminist philosophy
candidates.reason: Feminist and gender philosophy remains independently evidenced. Ethics, social theory and media provide partial contributions, but no additional programme is constructed after the maximum of three.

routeSelection.basis: Ordinary examination route with the maximum genuinely open elective option. Four modules are instantiated neutrally in their offered semesters from the first listed distinct entries; not chosen to inflate UCR correspondence. Current annual rules apply; no future-year offering guarantee.

selection.assessment: Three coherent responses retain a substantial philosophical foundation while differing in political/legal institutions, environmental/media applications, and mental-health/cognitive enquiry. The mental-health direction is newly supported by explicit current psychopathology, clinical and cognitive content rather than rejected on the absence of a single specialist title. Each pair must pass the qualitative and numerical distinctness checks; no fourth alternative is added.

notes.text: UCR combines philosophy and political theory with different applied fields: institutions and law, environmental communication and media, or mental health and cognitive science. Radboud has a 60 EC introductory philosophy year, later required courses and thesis, at least four complete philosophical modules, and 30 EC that may contain further modules or approved electives. These UCR programmes offer related academic study, not full module equivalence, credit-transfer advice or professional qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud’s Philosophy, Politics and Society programme studies philosophical ideas, arguments and their application to public problems. It combines historical and systematic philosophy, academic skills, thematic modules, a research project and a philosophical thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes combine sustained philosophy, political thought and AI ethics with different applications. One focuses on institutions, law and social research; another on environmental media, climate communication and governance; the third on mind, mental health and empirical enquiry. They offer less dedicated philosophical history, philosophy of science, metaphysics, textual methods and cumulative philosophical research than Radboud PPS. The mental-health route includes clinical psychology but confers no clinical qualification.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary PPS: four complete modules and 30 EC approved open electives
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC route shown contains 90 EC of compulsory foundations, later courses and thesis, four selected 15 EC modules, and 30 EC of approved open electives. Other complete modules may replace the elective space. Module choices shown are examples, not universal requirements. RADAr is mandatory without credit. Writing Workshop precedes Project; Project precedes thesis. Attendance and thesis-semester conditions apply. The first-year binding study advice threshold is 44 EC. UCR does not reproduce the PPS modules, confer this degree or guarantee master admission.

componentNotes.y2-project: A required philosophical research project. Students must first pass Philosophical Writing Workshop. Attendance is required; assessment includes individual literature work, a paper and presentation, plus a group thematic collection.
componentNotes.y2-module-1: Selected complete autumn module: Global Distributive Justice; Philosophy of International Law; Philosophies of War and Peace, each worth 5 EC.
componentNotes.y2-module-2: Selected complete spring module: Forms of Democracy; Who is the Demos; Counter-Democracy: Case Studies, each worth 5 EC.
componentNotes.y2-module-3: 15 EC of approved courses from other academic programmes. A complete PPS module may be chosen instead.
componentNotes.y3-practice: Professional reflection, career interviews and practical skills, documented in a portfolio. Attendance and a written task are required.
componentNotes.y3-module-1: Selected complete autumn module: History and Status of Psychiatric Illnesses; Neurodiversity; Mental health: philosophical, psychological or neuroscientific subject, each worth 5 EC.
componentNotes.y3-module-2: A second 15 EC elective block gives 30 EC of approved open choice overall. Complete PPS modules may be chosen instead.
componentNotes.y3-module-3: Selected complete spring module: Philosophy of Technology; Surveillance Society; Ethics of AI, each worth 5 EC.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: A required philosophical thesis of 5,000–6,000 words, following a passed Project course. It is normally completed in the second semester; first-semester participation requires the stated exchange, internship or adviser-consent conditions.
